overview: Two categories of point mutation that change a codon's meaning, one substituting an amino acid and the other creating a premature stop.
genZNote: Missense swaps one letter for another. Nonsense hits the eject button early.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A point mutation that changes a single codon to specify a different amino acid.
aspects.valueB: A point mutation that changes a codon into a premature stop codon.

aspects.label: Effect on Protein
aspects.valueA: Produces a full-length protein with one altered amino acid, which may or may not affect function.
aspects.valueB: Produces a truncated, usually non-functional protein, often degraded via nonsense-mediated decay.

aspects.label: Severity Spectrum
aspects.valueA: Ranges from silent/tolerated (conservative substitution) to severely disruptive, depending on the amino acid change and its location.
aspects.valueB: Generally more severe, especially if the truncation occurs early in the coding sequence.

aspects.label: Classic Example
aspects.valueA: Sickle cell disease: glutamic acid to valine substitution in beta-globin (a single missense mutation).
aspects.valueB: Certain forms of beta-thalassemia result from nonsense mutations that truncate beta-globin.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Changes the amino acid coded but preserves protein length.
aspects.valueB: Introduces a premature stop codon, truncating the protein.
